Theme

Latin word

fōrma

fōrma, fōrmae f.

noun, first declension

baking tin, mould; good looks, beauty; a design, an architect’s plan; form, shape, outward appearance; a format; the ideal form of a thing; a form; a version (of a text, a draft)

In this lexicon

    the recommended word · classical

  • beauty

    also used · classical · Ov. Ars 2.113; Hor. Ep. 1.4.6: dī tibi fōrmam … dederant (Lewis & Short)

  • design

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Q. fr. 2.5.3: quam quantum ex fōrmā jūdicābāmus; Cic. Fam. 2.8.1: cum fōrmam reī pūblicae vīderim, quāle aedificium futūrum sit scīre possim

  • form

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.35: tōtaque figūra et fōrma et statūra (Lewis & Short); Traupman 318

  • format

    the recommended word · modern · Traupman 261, 318

    also used · classical · Cic. Or. 43: excellentis ēloquentiae speciem et fōrmam adumbrābimus (Lewis & Short)

  • version

  • regiōnis fōrma: landscape

    * our formation

Notes

  1. 1fōrma: long o (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan 233–234, s.v. fōrma, prints the o long; Ernout–Meillet “stress the length of o”, which he takes for a recent lengthening of short o before r and a consonant (Leumann 1977: 114).
  2. 2fōrma: long o (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan 233–234, s.v. fōrma, prints the o long; Ernout–Meillet “stress the length of o”, which he takes for a recent lengthening of short o before r and a consonant (Leumann 1977: 114).

Examples

  • Fōrmās būtȳrō unguitō.

    Grease the tins with butter.Culīna Theodōrī

    In the entry for baking tin

  • fōrma bonum fragile est, quantumque accēdit ad annōs fit minor, et spatiō carpitur ipsa suō

    beauty is a fragile good: the more the years increase, the less it becomes, and it is worn away by its own spanOv. Ars 2.113–114

    In the entry for beauty

  • domus erit ēgregia; magis enim cernī jam poterat quam quantum ex fōrmā jūdicābāmus

    the house will be splendid: one can see more of it now than we could judge from the planCic. Q. fr. 2.5.3

    In the entry for design

  • nūdaque cōnsistunt, fōrmam servantia testae, vīna

    the wine stands bare, keeping the shape of its jarOv. Tr. 3.10.23–24

    In the entry for form
